title: Bin El Ouidane reservoir, 2 Sep to 26 Sep 2026
summary: From 2 Sep to 26 Sep 2026 the radar shows a lake that hardly changed, 29.75 km2 and then 29.82 km2. Mean HV over the circle did not move, with a change of 0.0 dB.

sections.heading: What changed
sections.text: The lake changed by 0.07 km2, or 0.2%, in 24 days. In HV, 0.32 km2 turned brighter by more than 3 dB and 0.21 km2 darker. Mean HH fell by 0.1 dB, with 0.44 km2 brighter and 0.28 km2 darker in HH.

sections.heading: Where, by terrain type
sections.text: Trees, shrub and rugged slopes had 0.11 km2 brighter and 0.08 km2 darker in HV. The changing fields type rose by 0.42 dB in HV and 0.41 dB in HH on average. Rough dry ground and fields had 0.07 km2 brighter and 0.05 km2 darker in HV.

sections.heading: Possible causes
sections.text: Possible cause for the steady lake: releases for irrigation balanced by inflow, or little use of the reservoir at that time; the dam's release record would show which. Possible cause for the changing fields: young crops growing; a field visit would check it.

sections.heading: Limits
sections.text: Neither date carries a flag. Lake areas are approximate: 8.6% and 9.2% of the outline falls on land in the optical photo. One track only, so slopes facing away from the radar can fall in shadow.

sections.heading: What an agency could do next
sections.text: Use this pair as evidence of a stable reservoir in September. Check the dam's records to see whether releases stopped or were balanced by inflow.
